title: Telemetry watchdog Terraform module for VPC observability: Prometheus/Grafana, OTEL, log-shipping
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Scope: Implement an opinionated, reusable Terraform module (V1) to provision and manage the full observability stack inside customer VPCs for Redwood Private installs. The module must support: (a) Prometheus + Thanos sidecar (or long-term remote write) with tenant-aware scrape configs, (b) Grafana deployment with datasource provisioning and dashboard bootstrapping, (c) OpenTelemetry Collector as a clustered, autoscaled service for metrics/traces/logs with stable endpoints, (d) log shipping pipeline to S3/Vector/Fluent Bit forwarder, and (e) lifecycle hooks for upgrades, maintenance drains, and graceful rollout/rollback.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include creating bespoke Grafana dashboards—we will seed a minimal set and link to a companion dashboards repo. It also does not cover RBAC integration beyond basic service account roles; advanced KMS/HSM integration is a follow-up.

Requirements/Constraints:
- Works for EKS-based Private deployments; module should be cloud-agnostic where reasonable but may include EKS-specific manifests/glue.
- Must be consumable as a terraform module with clear inputs/outputs and documented examples (single-tenant and multi-tenant VPC examples).
- Upgrades must be safe for customer data plane: include canary deployment strategy for collector and Grafana, Prometheus rollout with remote write buffer draining and WAL preservation, and logshipper graceful drain.
- Healthchecks: both Kubernetes-level readiness/liveness and module-level probes exposed to our control plane (HTTP health endpoints, prometheus scrape targets, and a small reconcile loop that reports status to STS).
- Failure modes: automatic rollback when upgrade failures exceed thresholds; fallback to a lighter collector config (e.g., cpu-only pipeline) if OOM occurs.

Implementation notes/approach:
1) API: terraform module with submodules (helm_release wrappers + k8s manifests templated via helm values). Inputs: cluster_id, namespace, prometheus_retention_days, grafana_admin_user, s3_log_bucket, remote_write_endpoint, otel_image_tag, log_shipper_image_tag, canary_percentage, health_probe_slo_ms. Outputs: prometheus_endpoint, grafana_endpoint, otel_ingest_endpoint, module_status_url.
2) Helm upgrades: use helm_release resource with automatic canary by deploying a second, small release (collector-canary) and traffic split via Service subset + weighted Envoy/ServiceMesh OR by toggling ConfigMap-based sampling and a small percent of traffic via Kubernetes patch. We will implement a simple canary that spins up a canary deployment with identical config and a Kubernetes Service that routes X% of synthetic probes.
3) Drain and WAL handling: Before removing Prometheus binaries during upgrade, snapshot WAL and push to S3 (or handoff to Thanos). For log shipping, use preStop hooks and a drain window (configurable) where the sidecar buffers to disk and flushes to S3.
4) Health orchestration: Terraform will create a small health-controller (deployment) that runs an internal reconciliation loop (stateless, lightweight) to verify scrape targets, collector ingestion, and log shipper delivery. The controller writes status to a custom k8s CRD (ModuleStatus) consumed by our console (this ticket only creates the CRD and controller; console consumption is follow-up).
5) Observability of the observability stack: enable internal metrics from collector/prometheus/grafana (exposed via ClusterIP + ServiceMonitor) and create a default alert rule set for SLOs (ingest-latency, scrape-failure-rate, log-drop-rate).

Acceptance criteria:
- terraform module deploys a reproducible stack into a test EKS cluster using the example config in the repo.
- Canary upgrade path exercised and automated rollback triggered in simulated failure (test harness simulating OOM in collector).
- Health-controller exposes ModuleStatus with states: Healthy, Degraded, Failed.
- Prometheus remote_write works end-to-end to a test remote endpoint and WAL snapshot/restore verified.
- Documentation: README with inputs/outputs, example usage, and an upgrade runbook.

Risks: bucket permissions for WAL snapshotting, complexity of safe Prometheus upgrades, and possible vendor lock-in depending on Thanos vs remote_write approach. Mitigation: default to remote_write with retention handoff and keep Thanos optional behind a flag.

notes: Keep module opinionated but with flags to turn off features (thanos, remote_write, grafana). Aim for an MVP that is secure by default (least privilege IAM, S3 encryption, minimal open ports).
testing_plan: Automated integration tests run in CI: deploy module to ephemeral EKS cluster (kind/EKS ephemeral in GH Actions), run canary upgrade, simulate OOM and verify rollback, run end-to-end remote_write and logshipper to S3. Add k6 synthetic traffic runner for ingest-latency tests.
rollout_plan: Stage -> Staging (internal) -> Customer preview (opt-in) -> GA. GA gated by 3 successful canary upgrade runs and one simulated failure rollback. Each stage has a playbook for manual rollback and contact list.
owner_notes: Coordinate with Platform (ENG-50987) for VPC networking changes and with Console team for ModuleStatus consumption. Expect follow-ups for RBAC hardening and KMS integration.
estimated_cost_impact: Low-to-medium: default configs aim for modest footprint; can increase with long retention or Thanos enabled.
